With the plan's 3600 s the need would be 4200 s = 70 min, and a pass started at PASS_DEADLINE 23:45 UTC plus 70 min ends 00:55, before DRIVER_END_BY 01:00 [campaign.sh:76-77], so under the plan's numbers the need gate never refuses a pass that PASS_DEADLINE allows. summary: ts() and past() are never validated at start, so a malformed NOT_BEFORE makes the NOT_BEFORE loop spin without sleeping and a DRIVER_END_BY in the past is only discovered after the machine was taken.
failure_scenario: Typo NOT_BEFORE=2026-09-20T05:00:00 Z: `date -d` prints nothing, past() fails with 'integer expression expected' (rc 2) so `! past` stays true, left becomes a negative number, `sleep -1789...` exits at once, and the loop writes a status line to status-history.log and .status many times per second until someone kills it (the NFS log grows without bound). With a stale exported DRIVER_END_BY=2026-09-20T01:00:00Z from tonight's shell, the Sunday run sleeps, waits for the lease, takes the marker, installs the base deb and writes config.env, and only at line 458 stops with 'not enough time before DRIVER_END_BY' and restores: a lost day.
fix: After line 86 add: `for v in NOT_BEFORE DEADLINE_START PASS_DEADLINE DRIVER_END_BY; do [ -z "${!v}" ] && continue; ts "${!v}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "$v='${!v}' does not parse"; exit 64; }; done; past "$DRIVER_END_BY" && { echo "DRIVER_END_BY $DRIVER_END_BY is in the past"; exit 64; }` and in the NOT_BEFORE loop guard `[ "$left" -gt 0 ] || left=60`.

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED in substance, with two corrections to the scenario and three to the fix.

Scenario part 1 (malformed NOT_BEFORE spins): the mechanism is real but the reviewer's example is wrong. On the client host GNU date parses "2026-09-20T05:00:00 Z" to 1789880400 (= 2026-09-20T05:00:00Z), rc 0, so that typo works as intended. A genuinely unparseable value is needed (measured rc 1 for "2026-09-20T0500Z", "2026-09-20T05:00:00ZZ", "2026-09-2005:00:00Z", "2026-09-20T25:00:00Z"). With such a value the code as written does spin: ts() [campaign.sh:110] prints nothing, past() [:111] runs `[ now -gt "" ]` -> "integer expression expected" rc 2, so `! past` at :339 stays true; `left` at :340 becomes -1789854668 (measured); `sleep "$left"` at :341 fails at once ("sleep: invalid option -- '1'", rc 1); three iterations took 12 ms, each writing .status and appending to status-history.log [:92]. Extension not in the finding: a malformed DEADLINE_START or PASS_DEADLINE makes past() return 2 (= false), so every deadline guard (:348, :356, :361, :364, :376, :380, :449, :450) is silently disabled and the lease/flock/marker waits become unbounded.

Scenario part 2 (DRIVER_END_BY already in the past): confirmed. Nothing validates it; its first read is in run_pass [:249-250] or at :458. Both come after launch.sh took Bill's marker [launch.sh:44-47], after the preflight and deb saves [:386-399], and after hwattn-off wrote USE_HW_ATTN=0 to config.env [:405-406]. With CHECK=1 (default) it also comes after switch_to canon [:411] (canon installed, engines restarted); run_pass then returns 3, check_verdict [:274-285] maps rc 3 to "unknown", run_check [:302-310] restarts the engines and repeats, gets 3 again, and the campaign stops via stop_safely with the misleading record "check 8u x 8192 failed twice for reasons unrelated to the prompt length (rc 3 ...)" [:431]. With CHECK=0 the stop is at :458 as the reviewer states. Either way the restore runs correctly, but the Sunday window is lost and the log names the wrong cause. The trigger needs an operator error (the plan gives different DRIVER_END_BY values for tonight and Sunday, so the value must be changed between launches), which is why low/medium, not high.

Proposed fix problems: (1) "after line 86" is BEFORE ts()/past() are defined [:109-111]; a call to an undefined function returns 127, the `||` branch reads that as a parse failure, and EVERY launch would exit 64 (verified with a bash -c reproduction: prints "does not parse", rc 64). (2) A bare `exit 64` after launch.sh took Bill's marker leaves the marker taken; only release_lock runs on EXIT [:241]; the file's own rule says any early exit must go through abort_early [:240-242]. (3) Placed before :334 the check also runs when unit tests source the file with CAMPAIGN_LIB_ONLY=1, and `exit` would kill the test shell once the default dates are in the past. Note (not part of the fix): the client host runs in PDT, so a value without a zone suffix is read as PDT (7 h later in UTC); the parse check does not catch that.
verdict.corrected_fix:
campaign.sh: insert AFTER line 334 (`[ "${CAMPAIGN_LIB_ONLY:-0}" = 1 ] && return 0`) and BEFORE the `status "campaign start ..."` line 335 (ts/past are defined by then; unit tests never reach it; abort_early releases Bill's marker and writes outcome.txt/.done-aborted):

for v in NOT_BEFORE DEADLINE_START PASS_DEADLINE DRIVER_END_BY; do
  [ -z "${!v}" ] && continue
  ts "${!v}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || abort_early "$v='${!v}' does not parse as a time (date -u -d); use the form 2026-09-21T01:00:00Z" 64
done
for v in DEADLINE_START PASS_DEADLINE DRIVER_END_BY; do
  past "${!v}" && abort_early "$v=${!v} is already in the past (stale value from an earlier launch?)" 64
done
[ "$(ts "$DEADLINE_START")" -le "$(ts "$PASS_DEADLINE")" ] && [ "$(ts "$PASS_DEADLINE")" -le "$(ts "$DRIVER_END_BY")" ] || abort_early "deadlines out of order: need DEADLINE_START <= PASS_DEADLINE <= DRIVER_END_BY" 64

Optional belt-and-braces in the NOT_BEFORE loop (line 340), only for the race where NOT_BEFORE passes between the past test and the ts call: `[ "$left" -gt 0 ] || left=1`.

launch.sh: add the same checks BEFORE the TAKE_MARKER block (before line 44), so the operator sees the error synchronously and nothing is taken (launch.sh has set -u and no ts/past, so use date directly and ${!v:-}):

for v in NOT_BEFORE DEADLINE_START PASS_DEADLINE DRIVER_END_BY; do
  [ -z "${!v:-}" ] && continue
  date -u -d "${!v}" +%s >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "$v='${!v}' does not parse as a time; use 2026-09-21T01:00:00Z form"; exit 1; }
  case $v in DEADLINE_START|PASS_DEADLINE|DRIVER_END_BY) [ "$(date -u +%s)" -gt "$(date -u -d "${!v}" +%s)" ] && { echo "$v=${!v} is in the past"; exit 1; };; esac
done

Then re-run the md5 sync check of launch.sh (both files change) and `bash -n` before launching.

summary: When hwattn-clear fails, the handoff takes production down only (correct), but the config.env byte count is read AFTER that decision (lines 214-216); a failed clear on a file that is already 0 bytes (hwattn-off never wrote it) therefore leaves production down although the end-state condition is met.
failure_scenario: Line 407: sudo -n tee is refused, hwattn-off exits 1, HWATTN_SET stays 1, stop_safely runs restore_and_release. Line 197: sudo -n truncate is refused too, HWATTN_SET stays 1. Line 207-209: production is taken down and not brought up. Line 215 then reads 0 bytes and says 'config.env is 0 bytes (ok)'. Result: config.env clean, restore-target deb installed, production engines down until jhan runs serving-up by hand.
fix: Move the cfgbytes read (lines 214-216) to just after the hwattn-clear block (after line 199) and treat a read of 0 as cleared: if [ "$HWATTN_SET" = 1 ] && [ "$cfgbytes" = 0 ]; then HWATTN_SET=0; say "hwattn-clear failed but config.env reads 0 bytes: treating it as cleared"; fi, so the up-path condition at line 203 holds.

verdict.reason: Confirmed with the code as written, with one correction to the failure chain. Evidence: campaign.sh:406 raises HWATTN_SET=1 before the write; campaign.sh:407 sends hwattn-off, and dut.sh:126 exits 1 when `sudo -n tee` fails, so the file stays at the 0 bytes that preflight proved (campaign.sh:395). stop_safely (campaign.sh:317-322) calls restore_and_release. There, HWATTN_SET is reset to 0 ONLY by a successful hwattn-clear (campaign.sh:197); dut.sh:132 exits 1 when `sudo -n truncate` fails, so HWATTN_SET stays 1. ensure-base (dut.sh:100-103) finds the restore target still installed and exits 0 without sudo, so restored=1. The up path at campaign.sh:203 needs HWATTN_SET=0 and is skipped; the elif at 207-209 runs serving-down only. The plain-stat read that would prove the file empty comes only at campaign.sh:214-216, after the decision, and prints "config.env is 0 bytes (ok)". The plan (section 2 end state, 2a "stop safely" bullet, section 4 step 3) requires HANDOFF=up after a cleared config.env and does not decide the case "clear command failed but the file is verifiably empty", so the "down only" outcome is the script's choice, not a plan decision. Correction to the scenario: if sudo -n is refused for ALL commands (the most likely single cause of both tee and truncate failing), serving-down does not take production down either: dut.sh:159 `sudo -n journalctl` fails 12 times and dut.sh:167 exits 1 before the POST /api/inference/down, so production stays up with the correct binary and an empty config.env, and the record says HWATTN-CLEAR-FAILED + HANDOFF-INCOMPLETE (a misleading record, medium by the task's scale). The reviewer's exact outcome (production down, config.env clean, restore target installed, up only when jhan or the 02:45 UTC ci-runner-stop brings it up) occurs when only the write to config.env fails while sudo works (read-only or immutable file, per-command sudoers). Either way the decision at line 203 ignores the observable file state. The proposed fix is right in principle (treat a plain-stat read of exactly 0 as cleared) but incomplete: moving lines 214-216 forward removes the final post-serving-up check that plan section 4 step 3 requires ("final stat -c %s config.env = 0" as the last step), and the status text at line 198 and the header lines 26/44 would then be wrong. Add a fallback read in the failure branch instead and keep the final read.

summary: The header says `kill -TERM <pid>` stops the campaign, but bash runs the TERM trap only after the current foreground command ends, so during `sleep 1800` (lines 341, 377) or `sleep 120` (349, 357, 381) the stop is deferred by up to 30 min.
failure_scenario: Sunday 14:00Z, the operator decides to stop the run while it waits for Bill (`sleep 1800` at line 377). kill -TERM is sent; nothing happens until the sleep ends up to 30 min later; the operator sends kill -9, which skips restore_and_release and leaves the flock holder, the marker and (after hwattn-off) config.env in place.
fix: Replace the foreground sleeps in the wait loops with `sleep "$left" & wait $!` (a `wait` builtin returns at once when a trapped signal arrives), or define `nap() { sleep "$1" & wait $!; }` and use it at lines 341, 349, 357, 362, 377, 381.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on the bash semantics, with two corrections to the scenario's consequences. (1) Mechanism: bash 5.1.16 runs a trapped signal's handler only after the current foreground command ends; the `wait` builtin instead returns at once. Measured in the scratchpad: a script with `trap ... TERM` and a foreground `sleep 6` got TERM at t+1.0 s and ran the trap at t+6.0 s (after the sleep ended); the same script with `sleep 6 & wait $!` ran the trap 1 ms after the kill. So `kill -TERM <pid>` (header line 39) is deferred by up to 30 min while campaign.sh sits in `sleep "$left"` (line 341, left capped at 1800) or `sleep 1800` (line 377), by up to 2 min in the `sleep 120` loops (lines 349, 357, 381) and 1 min at line 362. During a pass the header claim holds: run_pass waits with `wait "$DRIVER_PID"` (line 262), which returns at once on TERM. The plan decides nothing about stop latency (sections 2, 2a, 10 read). (2) Corrections: every one of the six sleeps runs BEFORE hwattn-off (line 407), so a kill -9 there cannot leave config.env written; and at line 377 Bill's marker is PRESENT (bill take returned rc 2 = Bill active), so there is no marker of ours to release. The real consequence of an escalated kill -9 during those waits is: the remote flock holder `sleep 50400` (hold_lock line 119, taken at line 360 before the marker loop) stays for up to 14 h, no .done-* file and no outcome.txt are written, and launch.sh's pgrep gate then allows a second launch that fails at hold_lock. After hwattn-off the remaining deferral windows are the foreground `timeout N ssh` dut.sh steps (serving-down 1500 s, ensure-*/serving-up 900 s, verify-env 300 s), not sleeps; making those interruptible would be wrong (the restore would then issue its own serving-down while the interrupted one still runs on the DUT), so they should be documented, not changed. Severity stays low/medium: the header's stop instruction is misleading about latency, and the wrong machine state needs an operator to ignore its "NOT -9" line.

summary: The runtron gate 'until ! timeout 60 ssh ... pgrep ...' treats an ssh failure (rc 255, or 124 on timeout) the same as 'no process found', so an unreachable DUT passes the gate and line 359 logs 'no runtron process on the DUT'.
failure_scenario: DUT reboots at the moment of the gate: ssh returns 255, '!' makes it true, the loop ends, status says no runtron process. hold_lock then fails for 60 s and loops on the deadline, so the consequence is a misleading status line, not a wrong action.
fix: Capture the remote pgrep status explicitly: while :; do r=$(timeout 60 ssh $SSH_OPTS "$DUT_ALIAS" "pgrep -u jhan -f '[r]untron[. ]|[i]ssue4500.*campaign[.]sh' >/dev/null; echo \$?" 2>/dev/null); [ "$r" = 1 ] && break; past "$DEADLINE_START" && abort_early ... 3; status "waiting: ${r:+another campaign runs on the DUT}${r:-DUT did not answer the runtron check}"; sleep 120; done.

verdict.reason: Confirmed at low severity. Code as written [campaign.sh:355]: `until ! timeout 60 ssh $SSH_OPTS "$DUT_ALIAS" "pgrep ... >/dev/null"`. pgrep returns 1 when no process matches (verified locally), ssh returns 255 when it cannot connect, timeout returns 124. `!` maps every non-zero status to true, so rc 255 and rc 124 end the until-loop exactly like rc 1 (verified: `until ! (exit 255)` skips the body). Line 359 then logs "no runtron process on the DUT" although nothing was checked. Follow-on: hold_lock's background ssh dies within ConnectTimeout=20 s, `kill -0 $LOCK_PID` fails, the loop breaks, and the else branch at line 133 logs "campaign flock on the DUT is HELD by another campaign: ssh: connect ..." (a second misleading line), so the loop at 360-363 waits on the deadline; no package or engine action happens before the DUT answers. In the reviewer's scenario (DUT reboot) no runtron process survives the reboot, so the consequence is only the misleading record. A wrong action (our campaign taking the flock between a peer's runtron runs) would need a transient ssh failure at the gate AND a running peer campaign; the plan states the peer campaign issue4500-m6 finished 18:40 UTC with its .done marker present [plan lines 82-84], and launch.sh lines 38-39 refuse to launch while the marker is missing or the pgrep matches, so that scenario is outside the plan's stated state. The proposed fix is wrong in its message: with r=0 (a match) `${r:-DUT did not answer...}` expands to "0", so status prints "another campaign runs on the DUT0" (verified locally); this is the header's own trap "never ${VAR:+x} with a 0/1 flag" [campaign.sh:58]. pgrep rc 2/3 would also print a garbled line. Use a case statement on the remote status instead (corrected fix below).
verdict.corrected_fix:
Replace campaign.sh lines 355-359 with a loop that reads the remote pgrep status explicitly and names each case:

# another session's campaign (runtron cells on our half, e.g. issue4500-20260918) may run without holding the campaign
# flock: wait until no runtron process and no other campaign.sh of ours runs on the DUT (2026-09-19 13:45 UTC coordination).
# The remote pgrep status is echoed and read here: an ssh failure (rc 255) or a timeout (rc 124) must NOT pass the gate.
while :; do
  r=$(timeout 60 ssh $SSH_OPTS "$DUT_ALIAS" "pgrep -u jhan -f '[r]untron[. ]|[i]ssue4500.*campaign[.]sh' >/dev/null; echo \$?" 2>/dev/null); src=$?
  case $r in
    1)  break;;                                                        # pgrep: no process matched
    0)  msg="another campaign (runtron) is running on the DUT";;
    "") msg="the DUT did not answer the runtron check (ssh rc $src)";;
    *)  msg="the runtron check returned pgrep rc $r";;
  esac
  past "$DEADLINE_START" && abort_early "past DEADLINE_START while waiting for another campaign's runtron processes to end ($msg)" 3
  status "waiting: $msg"; sleep 120
done
status "runtron check: no runtron process and no other campaign.sh of ours on the DUT"

Notes: (1) `r=$(...); src=$?` captures the ssh/timeout status of the command substitution, which is 255 or 124 when the DUT did not answer and r is empty. (2) No `${r:+...}`/`${r:-...}` on a 0/1 value (header trap, line 58). (3) Optional, same class: hold_lock line 133 labels an ssh connect failure as "HELD by another campaign"; test `grep -q '^ssh:' "$RES/.lock.out"` first and say "hold_lock: ssh failed: ..." in that case.

summary: kill -TERM during a foreground sleep is deferred by bash until the sleep ends, so the header's 'TO STOP EARLY: kill -TERM' waits up to 30 min in the marker loop (sleep 1800) and up to 30 min in the NOT_BEFORE loop (sleep $left, line 341); only the driver wait (line 262, builtin wait) reacts at once.
failure_scenario: Operator sends TERM at 22:05 UTC while line 377 sleeps until 22:34. on_signal runs at 22:34; meanwhile the flock stays held and the status file still says 'waiting: Bill is active'.
fix: Use an interruptible sleep in the long waits: replace 'sleep 1800' (line 377) and 'sleep "$left"' (line 341) with 'sleep 1800 & wait $!' and 'sleep "$left" & wait $!' (wait returns when the trap fires; on_signal then exits).

verdict.reason: Confirmed with line evidence and a live test. (1) campaign.sh:377 runs `sleep 1800` as a foreground child inside the marker loop, and campaign.sh:341 runs `sleep "$left"` (capped at 1800 s, line 340) in the NOT_BEFORE loop. (2) The trap is `trap on_signal TERM INT HUP` (line 239); bash runs a trap only after a foreground child exits, and the script sets only `set -u` (line 62), nothing that changes this. (3) The operator instruction is `kill -TERM <pid of this script>` (header line 39), and launch.sh:46 starts the script with `setsid nohup bash campaign.sh ... &`, so the TERM reaches only the bash process, not the child sleep. (4) The marker loop runs after `until hold_lock` succeeded (lines 360-364), so the remote flock holder stays alive during the deferred 30 min, and `status` (line 92) last wrote "waiting: Bill is active" (line 377), which stays in .status until the sleep ends. (5) Only `wait "$DRIVER_PID"` (line 262) is a builtin wait and reacts at once, as the finding says. (6) Live test on the launch host (bash 5.1.16, scratchpad/trapdefer.sh): TERM sent at t=1 s into a foreground `sleep 8` -> trap ran at t=8 s; with `sleep 8 & wait $!` -> trap ran at t=1 s, but the detached `sleep 8` stayed alive after the script exited. The plan (qwen3-4b-Saturday-plan.md) says nothing about the stop procedure, so this is not a plan decision; the same `sleep 1800` was already in .orig/campaign.sh:320 (inherited). Severity low stands: no DUT state has been changed yet at either sleep (install and config.env changes come after preflight, line 385+), the harm is a stop delayed up to 30 min, the flock held that long, and a stale status line. The proposed fix works for responsiveness but is incomplete: the trap's `exit 130` (line 237) skips the line after `wait`, so the detached `sleep 1800` survives the script for up to 30 min on the launch host.
verdict.corrected_fix: Add an interruptible sleep helper and kill its child from the trap. Near line 245 (after the traps, with the other globals): `SLEEP_PID=` and `isleep() { sleep "$1" & SLEEP_PID=$!; wait "$SLEEP_PID"; SLEEP_PID=; }`. Replace line 341 `sleep "$left"` with `isleep "$left"` and line 377 `sleep 1800` with `isleep 1800` (optionally also the 120 s / 60 s waits at lines 349, 357, 363, 380 for a stop within seconds instead of up to 2 min). In on_signal, right after `trap '' TERM INT HUP` (line 229), add `[ -n "$SLEEP_PID" ] && kill "$SLEEP_PID" 2>/dev/null` so the detached sleep does not outlive the script. `wait <pid>` waits for that one pid only, so it does not interfere with the background ssh flock holder (LOCK_PID, line 119) or the driver wait (line 262). Verified behaviour: TERM during `isleep` returns from `wait` at once (status >128), on_signal runs, kills the sleep, restores and releases; without a signal `isleep` returns 0 after the full time and the loop continues as before.

summary: save-base-deb deletes the existing saved file (rm -f $OUT/$file) before the replacement download has succeeded, so a call with a VERSION that differs from the saved copy and is no longer downloadable destroys the only local copy of the base arm's deb.
failure_scenario: An operator launches with EXPECTED_BASE overridden (or mistyped) to a version other than 2026.09.18-3faba6d0; campaign.sh:400 calls `save-base-deb <that version> nightly.deb`; the version check at line 95 fails, line 96 removes nightly.deb (137,845,288 bytes, the base arm), apt-get download fails because Monday's publish-deb has dropped the version from the index (the header comment at lines 90-91 names this risk) and /var/cache/apt/archives has no copy -> exit 1 -> abort_early, but nightly.deb is gone; ensure-base for the real base arm later falls back to the repository, which may no longer index 2026.09.18-3faba6d0 either. The campaign's normal call passes the saved version and exits at line 95, so this is latent, not tonight's path.
fix: Download to a temporary name and replace only after the version check: `tmp=$OUT/.$file.tmp; rm -f "$tmp"; ( cd "$OUT" && apt-get download "tron=$want" ... && mv -f "tron_${want}_amd64.deb" "$tmp" ) || { c=...; [ -n "$c" ] && cp -f "$c" "$tmp"; }; [ -s "$tmp" ] && [ "$(dpkg-deb -f "$tmp" Version)" = "$want" ] || { rm -f "$tmp"; say ...; exit 1; }; mv -f "$tmp" "$OUT/$file"`. Drop the `rm -f "$OUT/$file"` at line 96.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as a latent low-severity defect; the code does what the finding says, but the plan's own path never reaches it.
